text: Commission the Natural Capital Committee to investigate the potential for other resource taxes, including deposit refund schemes.
explanation: An administrative instruction to commission an investigation into resource taxes and deposit refund schemes. Purely technical policy machinery with no moral language.

text: Fianna Fáil conducted the biggest ever reform of Civil Defence and the Army Reserve.
explanation: A descriptive claim about past reforms of Civil Defence and the Army Reserve. It reports an administrative accomplishment without evaluative or moral terminology.

text: Ensure that the Marine Institute has the necessary resources to be at the cutting edge of international marine research,
explanation: A commitment to resource the Marine Institute for cutting-edge research. Per the negative clarification, scientific research commitments are excluded absent moral framing.

text: We can reach that great goal of full employment.
explanation: An aspirational economic goal of full employment. 'Great goal' is rhetorical emphasis, not an ethical concept; full employment is presented as an economic objective, so it is coded 0.

text: Every element of America's homeland security plan is critical, because the terrorists are ruthless and resourceful - and we know they are preparing to attack us again.
explanation: Describing terrorists as 'ruthless' is an evaluative moral character judgment (ruthlessness being the absence of compassion/pity), used to justify the security plan through moralized characterization of adversaries rather than purely technical threat assessment. This fits the codebook's inclusion of virtue/vice-based language, though I acknowledge ambiguity since it also functions as a security justification.

text: o  each minister should prepare and publish a statement of the skills and roles sought for each board.
explanation: An administrative governance recommendation that ministers publish statements of skills and roles for boards. Procedural in nature with no moral content.

text: We have had an unprecedented 16 years of continuous economic expansion.
explanation: A descriptive economic claim about 16 years of continuous expansion. Matches the negative example of growth-focused economic statements free from ethical judgments.

text: We want young New Zealanders to be able to join KiwiSaver and stay in it for their working lives.
explanation: A policy preference about young people joining and staying in KiwiSaver. A programmatic savings policy without moralized or evaluative language.

text: • It has been four years since the Maori Commercial Settlement Act was passed, and most iwi are yet to receive any form of settlement from the Crown.
explanation: A descriptive statement noting that most iwi have not yet received settlements four years after the Act passed. While it implies a grievance, it uses no explicit moral terminology (justice, rights, desert, fairness), so per the negative clarification it is coded 0. Some ambiguity exists as the implied criticism borders on a justice claim.

text: Those policies have placed the federal government in the driver’s seat,
explanation: A descriptive claim about federal government policy positioning. No moral or evaluative language is present.

text: This has resulted in increased pressure in the health system and failed outcomes for healthcare staff, patients and the public.
explanation: A descriptive critique of health system pressure and failed outcomes. It reports policy failure in performance terms without ethical concepts or moral judgment language.

text: •  More than two in every three New  Zealanders  does unpaid work outside their  own households.
explanation: A descriptive statistic about unpaid work prevalence. No normative or evaluative framing is applied.

text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: An administrative description of ACARA coordinating cadetships with state awards. Procedural educational policy, matching the negative examples.

text: That’s why President Obama and Democrats in Congress have enacted infrastructure investments that will
explanation: A descriptive statement about infrastructure investments enacted by Obama and Democrats. Infrastructure spending commitments are explicitly excluded by the negative clarification.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: A fiscal claim about increased early childhood education funding. Purely a spending figure, excluded by the negative clarification on fiscal spending descriptions.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: Calling Infrastructure Australia 'secretive' is an evaluative administrative/political critique, but it does not invoke ethical concepts like corruption, justice, or rights. It falls under the negative clarification's exclusion of generic political criticism. Borderline, but 'secretive' alone is insufficient moralization.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: A pricing policy statement about discounted rates for South Island users. Administrative/economic with no moral content.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: A descriptive criticism that Labor has done little public education on cleaner fuels. A performance critique without moralized language.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: A descriptive fiscal statistic about income tax rates in 1997. Matches the negative examples of purely economic/factual statements.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: A purely descriptive statement identifying the speakers as co-leaders of the Green party. No evaluative or moral content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: A technical environmental policy goal about aviation emissions and a zero-carbon target. Per the negative clarification, environmental protection goals without moralized framing are coded 0.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: A regional development policy about pursuing an 'alternative growth pole' along the Atlantic Corridor. Economic/planning language without moral rhetoric.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: 'New rights for patients' invokes rights-based language, framing entitlements in normative terms rather than purely administrative ones. The codebook's definition includes invocations of rights as moral rhetoric. Ambiguity exists since these are statutory healthcare rights rather than fundamental human rights.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: An economic argument that farm sector investment fails to recognise farmers' economic contribution. The appeal is to economic contribution, not to moral desert, dignity, or fairness, so it is coded 0.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: A descriptive acknowledgment that adoption costs can be high or prohibitive for families. A policy problem statement without explicit moral terminology or desert claims.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: A programmatic commitment to increase arts access for young people, 'particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds.' Although equity-targeted, it uses descriptive socioeconomic language rather than explicitly moralized terminology (equality, fairness, rights, desert), so per the negative clarification on generic social policy commitments it is coded 0.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: A purely programmatic directive about allocating spending to health and education. Per the negative clarification, fiscal spending commitments aimed at positive outcomes but lacking explicitly moralized language are coded 0.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A policy commitment on public ownership of rail services, framed in administrative/economic terms with no ethical or normative terminology (no fairness, justice, desert, or virtue language).

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: Technical commitment to support land managers in delivering ecoservices; purely administrative with no moral vocabulary.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Descriptive statement about services contributing to political and economic well-being; administrative framing without evaluative moral terms.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A bullet point describing an administrative problem (conflicting roles); purely descriptive with no normative content.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: Generic environmental aspiration to be a 'world leader'; per the negative clarification, generic commitments to positive outcomes (environmental protection) without explicit moralized language are excluded.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: Fragment about promised investment in hospital buildings; infrastructure spending with no moral rhetoric.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A rhetorical question fragment directed at Labor; contains no ethical concepts, duty language, or virtue appeals.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: A law-and-order commitment to 'crack down on domestic violence.' Although it targets a social harm, it is framed as an enforcement policy without explicit evaluative/normative terminology (no 'justice', 'intolerable', 'deserve'), so per the negative clarification it is coded 0.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: Programmatic commitment to roll out a fruit and vegetable promotion programme in schools; administrative, no moral framing.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: Administrative reporting requirement for boards; purely procedural.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Health policy expansion justified in utilitarian terms (recovery and return to work); no ethical or desert-based language.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: Resource reallocation for whānau development; administrative framing without moral terminology.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: Paid parental leave pledge framed as giving parents 'more choice'; a policy benefit statement without explicit normative or ethical evaluation.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: Fiscal prudence statement ('wise use of public dollars'); administrative efficiency, not moral duty or virtue.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A fiscal statistic expressed per household; purely economic framing as in the negative examples.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: The phrase 'proud reputation in peacekeeping' invokes national honor and civic virtue, aligning with the clarification's markers of virtue ideals (e.g., 'patriotism'). Ambiguous because it is embedded in a defence policy commitment, but the honor/pride framing pushes it beyond the purely technical.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Explicitly deploys ethical concepts listed in the clarification: a 'fair legal system' that 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians' — fairness, rights, and respect are key moral markers.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Pledges to 'eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system'; equality/inequality is an explicitly listed ethical concept in the clarification, making this a normative fairness claim rather than a purely technical tax measure.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a legal requirement ('enshrined in law') to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid; despite the word 'must,' the sentence is a factual statement about fiscal legislation, not a moral appeal, so it falls under the negative clarification on descriptive fiscal texts.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: Descriptive account of an MP introducing a housing bill; programmatic narrative without moralized evaluation.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: Spending commitment for aged care beds; purely programmatic.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Community policing reform framed as rebuilding partnership between Gardaí and communities; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is collaborative-governance language, not an ethical or virtue claim.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: Cutting government waste to save money; utilitarian fiscal framing.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational vision ('best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old') with no explicit ethical terminology such as dignity, desert, or justice; per the negative clarification, generic aspirational commitments are coded 0.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: Administrative reform of ministerial car entitlements; 'entitlement' here is procedural and no moral judgment is expressed.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: The attack centers on whether opponents can be 'trusted,' invoking honesty and integrity — civic virtues per the definition. It is a moral character judgment (analogous to the 'corruption' marker) rather than a technical critique.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Parliamentary procedure for selecting bills by lottery; purely procedural.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: Committing to commemorate the Easter Rising 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week' invokes honor, respect, and patriotic commemoration — virtue ideals listed in the clarification.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Immigration policy justified by economic needs; 'sensible' is pragmatic, not moral, language.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Administrative accountability framework for schools; 'right' here means appropriate, not a moral right.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Frames geopolitics as a moral struggle culminating in 'the victory of free nations in the War on Terror'; 'free nations' invokes freedom as a normative ideal and casts the conflict in good-versus-evil terms rather than purely strategic ones. Somewhat ambiguous given the historical-analytic framing, but the evaluative 'free nations'/'victory' language meets the definition.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: Procedural point about debate time; no moral content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Fisheries enforcement statement; 'poachers' denotes rule-breakers and the passage is framed as regulatory policing. Borderline because 'no room for' hints at intolerance, but overall it lacks explicit ethical evaluation and is treated as enforcement policy per the negative clarification.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: Claim of jobs created through housing upgrades; economic record-keeping with no moral language.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland; political/administrative goal without normative framing.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: 'Dysfunctional' is a performance-based critique of an administrative body, not a moral judgment; technical reform framing.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: Technical critique of waste-management strategy (scale, traffic, recycling conflicts); no ethical language.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Economic transition goal (prosperous, decarbonized economy); programmatic with no moral terms.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: Business competitiveness target; purely economic framing.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: The claim that a 'fair share' of revenue 'should be returned' to regions explicitly invokes fairness and a normative entitlement — key markers 1 and 2 in the clarification.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Descriptive statistics on sport participation and volunteering; no normative evaluation.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Recognition of Māori enterprise's contribution to the economy; economic framing without moral vocabulary.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement a named policy framework (the Military Covenant); the sentence itself contains no explicit moral terminology (no duty, desert, or honour language), so it is treated as a generic policy commitment per the negative clarification.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Critique of party-funding limits describing effects on smaller parties; no explicit fairness/justice terminology, so coded 0 despite the underlying democratic-reform context.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Explicitly invokes 'fairness' — a listed ethical concept — and accuses Mr Howard of having 'forgotten what fairness actually means,' a direct moral charge against an opponent.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: Programmatic pledge to develop parent education programmes; administrative.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: Trade enforcement pledge on anti-dumping; technical/economic with no moral language.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Defence resourcing to meet UN/EU peacekeeping obligations; 'obligations' here refers to treaty commitments, framed administratively without moral appeal.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Descriptive critique of administrative delays and litigation frequency; no moralized or evaluative ethical language.
